verses.text: A long time later, in the third year of the drought, the LORD's word came to Elijah: "Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain on the land."
So Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. The famine was very bad in Samaria.
Ahab called for Obadiah, the man in charge of his palace. Obadiah had great respect for the LORD.
When Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets, Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them in two caves, fifty in each, and gave them bread and water.
Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs and all the streams. Maybe we can find some grass to keep the horses and mules alive, so we will not lose all our animals."
So they divided the land between them to search it. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
As Obadiah was walking along, Elijah met him. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down with his face to the ground, and said, "Is it really you, my master Elijah?"
Elijah answered, "Yes, it is me. Go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"
Obadiah said, "What have I done wrong, that you are handing me, your servant, over to Ahab to be killed?

As surely as the LORD your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my master has not sent people to look for you. When they said, 'He is not here,' he made that kingdom or nation swear that they could not find you.
And now you tell me, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."'

As soon as I leave you, the LORD's Spirit will carry you away to who knows where. Then when I tell Ahab and he cannot find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have respected the LORD since I was young.
Has no one told you, my master, what I did when Jezebel was killing the LORD's prophets? I hid a hundred of the LORD's prophets in two caves, fifty in each, and gave them bread and water.
And now you tell me, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."' He will kill me!"
Elijah said, "As surely as the LORD of Armies lives, the God I serve, I will show myself to Ahab today."
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, "Is that you, the one who brings trouble on Israel?"
Elijah answered, "I have not brought trouble on Israel. You and your father's family have. You have turned away from the LORD's commands and followed the Baals.
Now send out word and gather all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Bring the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah, who eat at Jezebel's table."
So Ahab sent word to all the Israelites and gathered the prophets on Mount Carmel.

Elijah went up to all the people and said, "How long will you keep going back and forth between two choices? If the LORD is God, follow him. But if Baal is God, follow him." The people did not say a word.
Then Elijah said to them, "I am the only one of the LORD's prophets left, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.

Bring us two bulls. Let Baal's prophets choose one bull for themselves. Let them cut it into pieces and put it on the wood, but not light a fire. I will get the other bull ready, put it on the wood, and not light a fire either.
Then you call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD. The God who answers with fire is the true God." All the people answered, "That is a good idea."
Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one bull for yourselves and get it ready first, since there are so many of you. Call on the name of your god, but do not light a fire."

So they took the bull that was given to them and got it ready. Then they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon. They shouted, "Baal, answer us!" But there was no sound, and no one answered. They danced around the altar they had made.

At noon Elijah began to make fun of them. "Shout louder!" he said. "He is a god, isn't he? Maybe he is busy thinking, or he has gone off somewhere, or he is on a trip. Or maybe he is asleep and needs to be woken up!"
So they shouted louder, and they cut themselves with swords and spears, as they usually did, until blood flowed all over them.
Noon passed, and they kept on raving until the time of the evening sacrifice. But there was no sound, no answer, and no one paid any attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come here to me." All the people came close to him. He repaired the LORD's altar, which had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes descended from Jacob, the man the LORD had spoken to, saying, "Your name will be Israel."
With the stones he built an altar in the LORD's name. Around the altar he dug a ditch big enough to hold about fifteen litres of seed.
He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and laid it on the wood. Then he said, "Fill four large jars with water and pour it on the offering and on the wood."
He said, "Do it again," and they did it again. He said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.
The water ran down all around the altar, and he even filled the ditch with water.

At the time of the evening sacrifice, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and prayed, "LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things because you told me to.
Answer me, LORD, answer me, so these people will know that you, LORD, are God, and that you are turning their hearts back to you."
Then fire from the LORD fell and burned up the offering, the wood, the stones, and the dirt. It even dried up the water in the ditch.
When all the people saw this, they fell face down on the ground and cried, "The LORD is God! The LORD is God!"
Then Elijah said to them, "Grab the prophets of Baal! Do not let any of them get away!" They grabbed them, and Elijah took them down to the Kishon Brook and killed them there.
Elijah said to Ahab, "Go, eat and drink, because I hear the sound of heavy rain coming."
So Ahab went off to eat and drink. But Elijah climbed to the top of Mount Carmel. He bowed down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
He said to his servant, "Go up and look toward the sea." The servant went up and looked, and said, "There is nothing there." Seven times Elijah told him, "Go back and look."

The seventh time, the servant said, "I see a small cloud, as small as a man's hand, rising from the sea." Elijah said, "Go and tell Ahab, 'Get your chariot ready and go down before the rain stops you.'"
Very soon the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall. Ahab rode off to Jezreel.
The LORD's power came on Elijah. He tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.
